exam: TU assessment: 60% final examination set by the university, 40% internal (assignments, lab work, attendance).

units.title: Introduction to Statistics
topics: Eight reasons why every computing student needs statistics

sections.title: Eight reasons why every computing student needs statistics

summary: Statistics collects, organises, analyses and interprets data; it is powerful but limited to aggregates and can be misused.
Data are qualitative or quantitative and measured on nominal, ordinal, interval or ratio scales.
Primary data come from surveys, interviews, observation and experiments; secondary data from existing records; each has typical problems.

units.title: Descriptive Statistics
topics: Eight uses of averages and measures of spread
Other averages: geometric mean, harmonic mean and weighted mean
Moments, skewness, kurtosis and Chebyshev's inequality

sections.title: Eight uses of averages and measures of spread
Other averages: geometric mean, harmonic mean and weighted mean
Moments, skewness, kurtosis and Chebyshev's inequality

summary: Mean, median and mode locate the centre; quartiles, deciles and percentiles split the data.
Range, QD, MD, variance, standard deviation and CV measure spread; CV compares different data sets.
The median resists outliers; the standard deviation is the standard measure of spread.
GM suits growth ratios, HM suits rates over equal distances, the weighted mean handles unequal importance; moments give skewness and kurtosis, and Chebyshev's bound works for any shape.

units.title: Correlation and Regression Analysis
topics: Eight uses of correlation and regression
How good is the fit: r-squared, standard error of estimate and probable error
Partial and multiple correlation, and a warning about pooled data

sections.title: Eight uses of correlation and regression
How good is the fit: r-squared, standard error of estimate and probable error
Partial and multiple correlation, and a warning about pooled data

summary: Correlation measures linear association with r from −1 to +1; correlation does not prove causation.
Least squares regression gives the best-fitting line for predicting y from x; the two regression lines meet at the means and their slopes multiply to r^2.
r^2, the standard error of estimate and the probable error judge a fitted line; partial and multiple correlation handle a third variable; pooled data can mislead (Simpson's paradox).

units.title: Probability
topics: Eight uses of probability and distributions
More distributions, normal approximation and the central limit theorem

sections.title: Eight uses of probability and distributions
More distributions, normal approximation and the central limit theorem

summary: Probability follows the addition and multiplication laws; conditioning updates probabilities and Bayes' rule inverts them.
Binomial models fixed trials, Poisson rare events, normal measurements, which are standardised to Z for table lookup.

Expectation and variance follow linear rules; joint tables give marginals, covariance and an independence test; hypergeometric, geometric, uniform and exponential distributions complete the standard list; the CLT justifies the normal approximation.

units.title: Sample Survey
topics: Population and sample; census versus sample survey
Sample selection and determining the sample size
Eight rules of a good sample survey

sections.title: Population and sample; census versus sample survey
Sample selection and determining the sample size
Eight rules of a good sample survey

summary: A sample survey is faster and cheaper than a census; its quality depends on the frame, the design, the questionnaire, the sample size and the control of errors.
Sample size for a proportion follows n0 = fracz^2 p (1 - p)e^2 with a finite-population correction.
Sampling error is random and shrinks with n; non-sampling errors are systematic and need careful procedures.

Eight sampling designs and tools, and what each is used for

sections.title: Ratio and regression methods of estimation
Sampling distributions: z, t and χ²
Pictures of sampling designs and sampling distributions
Eight sampling designs and tools, and what each is used for
Hypothesis testing in full: errors, power and the standard tests

summary: SRS is the baseline; stratification gains precision from homogeneous strata; systematic sampling is simple but pattern-sensitive; cluster and multistage designs cut cost; PPS handles unequal clusters.
Ratio and regression estimators exploit an auxiliary variable.
The CLT justifies z ; t replaces z for small n with unknown σ ; chi^2 tests counts.

A complete hypothesis test states H0 and H1, fixes α, computes a statistic and concludes in words; Type I and II errors trade off, and power rises with sample size; paired, two-sample, variance and proportion tests extend the one-sample tests.

Pictures of ANOVA and experimental design
Eight uses of ANOVA and designed experiments
Latin square design and multiple comparisons

sections.title: The F statistic and its distribution
Pictures of ANOVA and experimental design
Eight uses of ANOVA and designed experiments
Latin square design and multiple comparisons

summary: ANOVA compares several means by splitting total variation into between and within parts and testing their ratio with the F distribution.
One-way ANOVA handles one factor; two-way ANOVA adds a blocking factor to reduce error.
A significant F says means differ somewhere; follow-up tests locate the difference.
A Latin square controls two nuisance factors with error d.f. (t - 1)(t - 2); ignoring the blocks can hide a real treatment effect; the LSD test compares individual means after a significant F.
